title: Hypoglossal Nerve Stimulation in Obstructive Sleep Apnea With Complete Concentric Collapse
official: Physiological and Anatomical Determinants of Hypoglossal Nerve Stimulation Outcomes in Complete Concentric Collapse Investigational Cohort
summary: This study examines how hypoglossal nerve stimulation affects breathing and sleep apnea in adults whose airway closes from all sides at the soft palate during sleep, a pattern called complete concentric collapse. Participants will receive an Inspire hypoglossal nerve stimulation implant and undergo sleep studies, questionnaires, and home monitoring. This use of the device is investigational. The study will measure changes in airway collapsibility, sleep apnea severity, device use, and safety through 12 months after implantation.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age ≥18 years.
* Diagnosis of obstructive sleep apnea with an apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) ≥15 events/hour, confirmed by attended in-laboratory polysomnography (PSG) before enrollment and implantation.
* Complete concentric collapse (CCC) of the soft palate on clinically obtained drug-induced sleep endoscopy (DISE).
* Otherwise considered an appropriate candidate for HGNS implantation by the treating surgical and sleep medicine team, aside from CCC status.
* Prior CPAP failure or intolerance, consistent with usual HGNS candidacy evaluation.
* Ability to provide informed consent.
* Willingness to undergo investigational HGNS implantation and required follow-up procedures under the research protocol.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Contraindications to HGNS implantation or conditions that, in the judgment of the treating clinicians or investigators, make investigational HGNS use unsafe or inappropriate.
* Central or mixed sleep apnea comprising \>25% of total respiratory events.
* Any unstable or uncontrolled medical condition that, in the judgment of the investigator, would increase procedural risk or interfere with study participation.
* Inability to safely undergo study procedures, including overnight sleep studies or physiological monitoring.
* Prior HGNS implantation.
* Pregnancy
